title: 7-round AES-256: XOR-improved MITM: selected subkeys

target.description: Reduced-round AES-256, with initial whitening. Section5's partial-decryption boundary uses the final-round byte positions; Section2 describes omission of final MixColumns. success.description: Conditional model for uniquely identifying168bits of selected round-key material: four whitening-key bytes, one round-one byte and sixteen final-round-key bytes. These are not independent master-key bits. Section5.3 stores S(f(i)) XOR S(f(0)) for i=1..255 and removes one guessed byte per target. Adopt the intended corrected factorization/coordinates, Equation7 correct-hit marginals for all four targets, availability of all already acquired n2 structures to every target, and the source matching-phase work model. Also adopt the wrong-sequence uniform law conditional on the precomputed setup; this is a heuristic model premise about AES, not proved by the following algebra. For any bijective byte S-box, each255-byte normalized signature has exactly256preimages among256-byte raw sequences, so the conditional uniform raw law induces a uniform2040-bit normalized law. A normalized table is an image of at most \(2^{200}/n_1\) raw function entries; duplicates can only reduce the image size. Its modeled wrong-hit upper bound per test is \(2^{-1840}/n_1\), not the basic256-byte value. At most \(4n_2 2^{72}\) potential target/guess tests give an aggregate false-hit term \(2^{-1766}n_2/n_1\). The same coefficient as the raw construction results from two separate8-bit changes, not transfer of its per-test probability. Combining this with four correct-hit miss marginals gives \(p_{\mathcal M,\mathrm{sel}}\ge\max\{0,1-4(1-n_1^{-1})^{n_2}-2^{-1766}n_2/n_1\}\). No inter-target or inter-guess independence is assumed; Equation7 within-target sampling assumptions remain. This stored complete-table member fixes n1=n2=1. The positive failure term remains symbolic, not rounded to100%. A nonempty finite table, positive integer n2 of usable structures and feasible query allocation are required. The model implication is exact within these premises; its interpretation for actual AES is heuristic. Existing source conflicts, finite-domain and native-cost limits remain. Master-key completion, raw/basic models, eight-round extensions and new WLH constructions are excluded.

evidence.interpretation: Derived conditional selected-material bound, not a probability printed for this improved variant. A bijective S-box makes raw-to-normalized sequence mapping256-to-one. Under the setup-conditional wrong-sequence model this gives2040uniform bits, at most2^200/n1 table images and2^-1840/n1 wrong-hit per test. A fixed superset of4*n2*2^72 tests yields2^-1766*n2/n1, then four right-sequence miss bounds are subtracted without assuming target independence. All targets use the same already acquired structure allocation. The Table1 sampled member uses its actual n1=2^n,n2=4*2^n curve and all original costs. This scoped implication supersedes earlier absence-of-aggregate-inference wording only for the stated conditional model; no author-reported unconditional rate, source-conflict resolution, extra queries or master-key completion is supplied.
